solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Stumped by athletes going topless — crackers!

parts.note: ST is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for stumped

indicators.note: going topless says the first letter of the word for athletes is lost

parts.note: runners are athletes on the track

explanation.surface: A bowler's wild over has batsmen stumped while athletes strip off, and the whole scene is crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crackers' looks like an adjective (mad) but is a plural noun: crackers are knockouts or beauties.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are informal nouns for something or someone exceptionally impressive or attractive.

clue.text: Feature showing line below crown of barnet?

indicators.note: in a down clue, the line piece sits underneath the other piece
the crown is the top of the head, so the top letter of the word barnet is taken

parts.note: the word supplies only its first letter here
a row is a line of things

explanation.surface: A face with a hairline sitting just under the crown of someone's hair.
explanation.walkthrough: BARNET is Cockney rhyming slang for hair (Barnet Fair), so the surface fits a forehead below the hair.
explanation.definitionFit: The forehead is one of the facial features, a part of the face.

clue.text: Upset person signing cheque payment

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: the drawer is the person who draws, i.e. signs, a cheque

explanation.surface: Someone writing out a cheque is distressed at having to pay.
explanation.definitionFit: A bounty or recompense is a sum given in return for a service.

clue.text: Old and bitter, occasionally admitting one's old

indicators.note: admitting means letting the next word inside
occasionally means taking only every other letter of the word bitter

parts.note: sole means one and only, single

explanation.surface: An elderly person, sour by nature, sometimes confesses to being old.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'one's' reads as 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something outdated is no longer in use, past its time.

clue.text: Authority imprisons single blokes for trial

indicators.note: imprisons means holding the following pieces inside

parts.note: an authority on a subject is an expert
I is the Roman numeral one
blokes are men

explanation.surface: The authorities jail unmarried men pending their trial in court.
explanation.definitionFit: A test conducted to see whether something works is a scientific trial.

clue.text: Cons bearing Conservative's buffoonery

indicators.note: bearing means carrying the next piece within

parts.note: the cons in pros and cons are the antis, those against

explanation.surface: Political opponents put up with a Tory's clowning.
explanation.definitionFit: Clownish capers and silly tricks are what buffoonery consists of.

clue.text: For openers, more bitter's consumed by empty soaks

indicators.note: consumed by means swallowed inside the other piece
empty means losing all the inside letters of soaks, leaving its outside pair

parts.note: tarter means sharper-tasting, more bitter

explanation.surface: Hard drinkers with nothing left down a sharper ale as their first round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bitter' suggests beer but is part of the comparative adjective 'more bitter'.
explanation.definitionFit: First courses of a meal, which open it, are its appetisers.

clue.text: Jeers being caught out in vacant slips

indicators.note: in places the following pieces inside the other
vacant means emptied of its middle, leaving the outer letters of slips

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
off can mean out, as in lights off

explanation.surface: A cricket fielder is mocked after a catch goes down among empty slip positions.
explanation.walkthrough: Slips is a cricket fielding position next to the wicketkeeper; here it only gives its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To mock or sneer at someone derisively is a matching verb for jeering.

clue.text: Packing container holds neat opener for gift

indicators.note: holds means containing the next piece

parts.note: a bin is a container
neat is an old word for cattle, of which an ox is one

indicators.note: the opener is the first letter of the word gift

explanation.surface: Wrapping a present in a box that holds a tidy little opener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat' looks like an adjective (tidy) but is the old noun for cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting things into cartons for transport is a way of packaging them.

clue.text: Small present that's sometimes seen around Christmas

parts.note: the present is now, this moment in time

explanation.surface: A modest gift that only turns up around the festive season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' reads as a gift but means the present time.
explanation.definitionFit: A white Christmas, with flakes falling, is an occasional seasonal sight.

clue.text: Top clubs admitting game win's sorry

indicators.note: admitting means letting the following pieces inside

parts.note: A1 means first-class, top, with the 1 read as the letter I
polo is a game played on horseback
to get something is to win it
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: Top golf clubs concede that a game victory is a regrettable affair.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'win's' reads as 'is', a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling or expressing regret makes someone contrite and remorseful.

clue.text: Ocean floor beginning to swallow sailor

indicators.note: to swallow means taking the next piece inside

parts.note: a seed is the beginning from which something grows
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: The ocean starts to engulf a seaman, who sinks to the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: The bottom of the sea is its ground or floor.

clue.text: People keeping diary about new stuff

indicators.note: keeping means holding the next piece inside

parts.note: human beings are people

indicators.note: about means surrounding the next piece

parts.note: a log is a diary or record

explanation.surface: Diarists record notes about fresh things in their journals.
explanation.definitionFit: One's possessions and gear are informally one's stuff.

clue.text: Cooks around fire evenly before temperature's hottest

indicators.note: before puts the first piece ahead of the next
around means wrapping round the next piece

parts.note: to fry is to cook, so fries means cooks

indicators.note: evenly picks the even-positioned letters of the word fire

explanation.surface: A chef fries food round a fire before the heat is at its highest.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'temperature's' reads as 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of an adjective for burning, flaming heat means most hot.

clue.text: Help to grip top for substantial food

indicators.note: to grip means holding the next piece inside

parts.note: SOS is the distress call for help
a lid is a top, as of a jar

explanation.surface: A cry for help to unscrew a lid to get at some proper food.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that is not liquid, eaten by a patient after soup or milk, is solid fare.

clue.text: Trim edges of delicate Cheddar with extra slice

indicators.note: edges of takes the first and last letter of each following word

explanation.surface: Cut the rind off a fine cheese and add another slice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link joining the third and fourth words.
explanation.definitionFit: To trim something is to cut it down, reducing it in size.

clue.text: Propagates vegetables taking last of dung

indicators.note: taking means absorbing the next piece inside

parts.note: beets are root vegetables

indicators.note: last of takes the final letter of the word dung

explanation.surface: Vegetables are grown by taking manure from the heap.
explanation.definitionFit: To father or give rise to offspring is to reproduce, propagate.

clue.text: Driving train circling points

indicators.note: circling means surrounding the next piece

parts.note: a string is a train or series, as of horses
E, east, is a compass point, so two points give a pair of Es

explanation.surface: A train travels round the points on a railway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'points' suggests railway track switches, but means compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: Guiding a vehicle's direction is what a driver does at the wheel.

clue.text: Show group of animals round a lake

indicators.note: round means surrounding the next pieces

parts.note: a herd is a group of animals

explanation.surface: A herd of animals is displayed around a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: To announce or signal a coming event is to foreshadow, indicate it.

clue.text: Left pail rotating in tree top

indicators.note: in puts the reversed pieces inside the tree

parts.note: a pine is a tree

indicators.note: rotating means the pieces are turned round and read backwards

parts.note: a can is a pail

explanation.surface: A bucket abandoned and spinning around in a treetop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rotating' reverses L and CAN to give NACL.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest point or summit is the peak, the top.

clue.text: Pill estimated to cover most sick

indicators.note: the words cover the answer, which runs across them

explanation.surface: A pill estimated to treat the most poorly patients.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of ill, informal and rare, means most unwell.

clue.text: Magazine, one providing gossip for the audience

indicators.note: for the audience means as heard by listeners, a homophone signal

parts.note: a tattler is a gossip, a teller of tales

explanation.surface: A magazine that is a gossip to its readers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tatler is a long-running British society magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tatler is a British glossy covering high society.

clue.text: Tent top's ends are articulated

indicators.note: articulated means spoken aloud, so the letters are pronounced as their names
the ends of the word top are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: The top ends of a tent are hinged or jointed.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'top's' reads as 'is'; the two letters spoken as names spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A conical Native American dwelling of poles and skins is a kind of tent.

clue.text: Characters backward in alphabet are, till informed!

indicators.note: backward says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Those who are backward with letters remain unlettered until taught.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'Characters backward in alphabet are, till informed', but the parse marks 'Characters' only; the whole clue describes someone unable to read.
explanation.definitionFit: People who cannot read or write are unschooled, lettered characters lacking letters.

clue.text: Clothes to show off after rejection

indicators.note: rejection means turning back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: to brag is to boast, show off

explanation.surface: Clothes worn to flaunt oneself after being turned down.
explanation.definitionFit: Attire, especially of a distinctive kind, is someone's dress or clothing.

clue.text: Swallow with stopper lifted

indicators.note: in a down clue lifted means written upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: a plug is a stopper, as in a bath

explanation.surface: Drinking straight from a bottle once the cork is pulled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallow' could be the bird, but here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a large mouthful hastily is to gulp it down, a quick swallow.

clue.text: American wise guys sharing special practices

indicators.note: sharing means the two words overlap on one letter, so a copy of it goes

parts.note: sages are wise men

explanation.surface: American know-alls swapping their particular methods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sharing' means the two pieces overlap on a single S rather than both keeping one.
explanation.definitionFit: Customary uses and habits of a community are its conventions or practices.

clue.text: Lodge in digs oddly, housing on good terms

indicators.note: housing means enclosing the next piece
oddly takes the odd-positioned letters of the word digs

parts.note: well in means on good terms with someone

explanation.surface: Taking strange lodgings while being on friendly terms with the landlady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lodge' looks like a verb with 'in', but it is the noun; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A lodge is a house or residence, a place where someone lives.
